mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over three months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.0% within the last three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals persistent labor market weakness, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE exceeds 8% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of periods where UNRATE stays above 8% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO is below its 12-month moving average for four months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a monetary policy tightening coinciding with rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed their 12-month averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports broader equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST exceeds its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST is above its 12-month moving average for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their 12-month averages indicates a labor market expansion with low unemployment, which supports consumer spending and corporate profitability, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and UNRATE both exceed their 12-month averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero when both PAYEMS and UNRATE exceed their 12-month averages in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in Real Personal Income (proxied by RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals weakening household purchasing power, which reduces demand for goods and services and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls below its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero when RSAFS is below its 12-month moving average for five months.
